author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
The advancement and diversification of Beijing’s anti-ship missile platforms have bolstered its denial capabilities in the first island chain and could divert US and allied navies from warfare in a Taiwan Strait contingency, according to analysts.
Last week, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV released a video of a Type 052D destroyer firing a YJ-20 hypersonic anti-ship missile from its vertical launch system, showcasing the People’s Liberation Army Navy’s increased ability to target surface...
title: How Beijing’s hypersonic ‘carrier killers’ could distract US forces in a Taiwan conflict

author: Fan Chen
description:
In a historic breakthrough, a Chinese-led international team of scientists has confirmed the existence of the glueball – a rare form of matter made entirely of force.
The finding was announced by a Chinese research team on Thursday at the International Conference on High Energy Physics in Natal, Brazil. Held every two years, the event features some of the most significant advancements in the field.
After 15 years of research, the team finally gathered definitive evidence of glueballs using the...
title: What is a glueball? Chinese-led team finds rare particle made entirely of force

author: Ling Xin
description:
Robot dogs could one day lead the way across the moon, patrolling research stations, scouting hazards and helping astronauts search for scientifically valuable rocks, according to a blueprint by researchers working on China’s lunar base.
The concept envisions three astronauts working alongside intelligent machines. As the crew explores the moon’s surface, one astronaut would direct two robot dogs across the landscape, while another collects rock samples and carries out detailed scientific...
title: China’s lunar research station could be guarded by robot watchdogs, space scientists say

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Taiwan’s leader rehearsed a late-night emergency evacuation during the island’s largest annual military exercise in response to growing concerns over potential “decapitation” strikes by the People’s Liberation Army, local media reported on Thursday.
Under cover of darkness on Wednesday night, William Lai Ching-te, wearing body armour and a helmet, was transported from his Presidential Office in a Clouded Leopard armoured vehicle to a secure command centre, in accordance with the long-standing...
title: Taiwan’s William Lai rehearses late-night emergency escape during military drill

author: Julie Zhang
description:
Global pharmaceutical giants are doubling down on investing in China’s fast-growing biotech companies given the sector’s huge room for valuation growth, according to speakers at the Global Health Summit, which concluded in Hong Kong on Saturday.
“Multinational pharmaceutical companies are shifting their business strategies in China away from asset-heavy operations,” said Xu Chenming, head of the healthcare group at Hong Kong-based Citic Securities.
“They are moving towards investing in companies...
title: Global pharma giants turn to Chinese biotech to tap innovation, valuation growth

author: Fan Chen
description:
Though the relationship between the Chinese and Indian governments has been thawing, Beijing has yet to win over the Indian public as it lacked a long-term strategy and communication channels, according to Chinese researchers.
Beijing needed to find common ground by expanding its bottom-up strategies as “a matter of urgency”, Zhou Qingan, dean of Tsinghua University’s school of journalism, and Li Yiming, a research assistant at the school argued in a recent article.
In a June paper published in...
title: Why Beijing struggles to win Indian hearts and minds despite diplomatic thaw

author: Meredith Chen
description:
Flights serving eastern China were disrupted on Saturday as Typhoon Dolphin approached the coast, with some services cancelled and airlines offering flexible rebooking and refund options for affected passengers.
Most of the typhoon-related flight disruptions have been reported at airports in the cities of Ningbo, Wenzhou, Taizhou, Hangzhou and Shanghai, according to Chinese media.
Some travellers also reported receiving notifications that flights to and from Shanghai on Sunday and Monday would...
title: Typhoon Dolphin causes flight chaos in China, with Shanghai set to enter danger zone

author: Holly Chik
description:
For centuries, the Yangtze River has been China’s vital lifeblood, yet its floods have claimed countless lives. To tame its waters, flood-control systems have evolved from ancient dykes to the engineering marvel of the Three Gorges Dam.
But a new study has uncovered a paradox: some human interventions may have inadvertently worsened the very flood risks they were built to mitigate.
“We show that flood frequency peaked during the Little Ice Age [1500−1850] … and that human interventions,...
title: Chinese scientists find some Yangtze flood controls may do more harm than good

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s plan to dissolve the pro-Beijing Chinese Unification Promotion Party (CUPP) has sparked controversy over whether the independence-leaning authorities are using security concerns to suppress political dissent.
The island’s interior ministry is seeking a Constitutional Court order to declare the CUPP unconstitutional and dissolve it, marking the first such action against a political party in Taiwan’s history.
“The CUPP has long been linked to organised crime, including cross-border...
title: Taiwan’s push to dissolve pro-Beijing party triggers political censorship debate
